findings.reason: a worker must choose between the test-compatibility rule (existing tests at tests/test_resume_sweep_needs_an_observed_death.py:276 and tests/test_resume_refuses_a_live_worker.py:302 match the sentence by substring) and the "never calls it live" rule, and whichever it picks the in-motion refusal either still reads to a coordinator as a stray live process to stop — the exact misreading §6 exists to remove — or breaks the stated test-compat claim; the plan should state which clause carries the unknown reading and whether the opening sentence is scoped to the two pid-live sites only.
findings.text: the changed paragraph says the in-motion composer must name the attempt's stream age and say "its liveness could not be read on this host", and that "It never calls the attempt live", but the unchanged deliverable at line 111 requires "The present sentence stays as the message's opening" at all three sites, and that sentence at resumption.py:1112 is "run '<id>' still has a live process; observe or stop it before resuming" — so the composed message both asserts a live process and disclaims any liveness reading, and the fifth case as written passes on either wording
